what: The golden suite for this op runs ~50 min (3.6k executed cells after SUPPORTED widening), far above the 10-min Bash tool cap; the prompt presents the runner as a plain foreground command. First attempt was killed by the cap and the run lost. Had to self-discover the detached setsid/nohup + poll pattern, and that kernel .cpp files must NOT be edited while a golden run is in flight (JIT compiles source per program against the already-imported Python descriptor -> CT-arg mismatch).
suggest: State in the verifier prompt: launch eval_test_runner.sh detached (setsid nohup ... > log &) and poll golden_results.txt; never edit kernel sources or the descriptor while a run is live; budget 3 runs (as-handed, post-fix, final).

what: An input(cb, WaitPolicy::None, ...) that addresses a tile the PREVIOUS eltwise_chain packed (PackTile default push) is a pack->unpack race: nothing but cb_wait_front orders the packer write against the next chain unpack. The helper docs describe None as caller-managed but do not warn that a same-kernel producer chain is not a valid manager; l1-footprint-discipline.md says it only for in-place transforms. Manifested as non-deterministic per-element errors on one layout/affine combination, took a bisecting probe to find.
suggest: Add to the WaitPolicy::None doc: if the tile was produced by a preceding chain in this kernel, cb_wait_front(cb, index+1) is mandatory before the consuming chain; consider a debug-build assert that a None-policy input CB has at least offset+1 tiles fronted.

what: The reference for bfloat8_b WEIGHTS is built from the bf16-rounded torch tensor while the device consumes bf8b-quantised values; fp32-activation x bf8b-affine cells therefore sit at rms 0.0093 against the fp32 target 0.01 purely from reference quantisation, a seed-flip risk unrelated to the kernel. Also bf8b padding semantics (shared exponent per 16-lane block) are documented nowhere in the layout references, yet garbage in pad lanes of a bf8b OUTPUT tile corrupts valid lanes.
suggest: Golden template: dequantise bf8b tensors for the reference via ttnn.to_torch of the device tensor (as done for activations). tensor_layouts / memory-layouts references: note that bf8b tiles share an exponent per 16-element row segment, so pad lanes of a bf8b output must be finite and small, not merely masked.
